title: Economies of scale and the value of automation

kcs.statement: Because AWS pools usage from hundreds of thousands of customers, it buys and runs hardware more cheaply than one company could, and passes the savings on as lower pay-as-you-go prices.
Automating provisioning and operations makes deployments repeatable and consistent, reduces human error, and cuts the staff time and cost of running workloads compared with one-time manual steps.

problem_ideas: AWS has cut prices many times since launch: which benefit explains this?
A team builds 12 identical test environments a month by hand with frequent mistakes: name two automation benefits.
Choose between a one-time manual setup and a repeatable automated process for a weekly environment rebuild.
Match the phrase 'aggregated usage from many customers' to the right benefit among four options.
A small company cannot negotiate hardware discounts: explain how the cloud gives it the same purchasing power.
Spot the distractor: 'Economies of scale means your application scales automatically.'
